pull.title: refactor: Enable more tidy bugprone checks
pull.body:
Enable some bugprone clang-tidy checks, which seem useful.

Apart from a test-only bug, they didn't find anything severe, but I think it still makes sense to enable them, so that it is easier to read the resulting code. Also, it is trivial to disable them, if they turn out annoying.

comments.body:
> [fa077e9](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36588/changes/fa077e9f79b9d5533991e208ad25e35474ed4ca2) _refactor: Enable bugprone-inaccurate-erase_:

What do you mean by this?

> Note: Wallets are unique, so the code change does not change any
behavior.

https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/container/vector/erase2 seems to specify that they are equivalent.

> https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/container/vector/erase2 seems to specify that they are equivalent.

Heh, the docs say that

std::erase(c,v);

is equivalent to

c.erase(std::remove(c.begin(), c.end(), value), c.end());

However, the code here is:

m_wallets.erase(std::remove(m_wallets.begin(), m_wallets.end(), wallet_model)); // note the "missing" end


This is harmless in this case, but confusing, because:

* It doesn't follow the idiom.
* Apparently reviewers (including myself) aren't familiar with the idiom, unless they look it up.

So my recommendation would be to completely get rid of std::vector::erase and instead use the C++20 std::erase(vector,...)

Dang, missed it. :D

nit: The commit message could be made clearer:

> Note: Wallets are unique, so even through we previously weren't specifying a range of iterators to vector::erase(), the behavior does not change.

> nit: The commit message could be made clearer:

Thx, will leave this thread open for now, so that reviewers see it, and so that I can avoid a push and review churn.
